_comment: TOML batch-writer vectors, replayed by _shared/lua/test/toml_batch_write_vectors_contract.lua on macOS and Linux. Each vector gives the file bytes (source; "" is an empty file), the batch rows and what the writer's prepare step must answer without publishing. The entry point is the batch writer's prepare step: given the source bytes and the rows, it answers accepted or refused, a detail, and the candidate bytes. expect.ok is acceptance; content is the exact candidate bytes; unchanged means the candidate equals the source; decoded lists TOML paths (array of keys) whose decoded value must equal value (a JSON null is not used); contains and not_contains are substrings of the candidate; detail_contains are substrings of the refusal detail; reads is the number of times the source may have been read (0: refused before reading). A row value {"$number": "text"} is the number the text spells (IEEE: "-0.0" is negative zero), which JSON cannot carry. Converted from toml_batch_existing_key_contract.lua and toml_quoted_headers_contract.lua; the ledger in contract_conversion_ledger.json records which cases moved. expected_snapshot (optional) is the caller's earlier read {status, content}: when the source read now differs the writer refuses with "source changed before preparing the batch"; expect.detail_equals is the exact refusal detail.
entry_point: batch writer prepare step: prepare_batch(path, rows, {read source}) -> accepted, detail, candidate bytes

drivers.windows: Not ported: one AHK consumer must call the Windows batch writer's prepare step on (source, rows) and compare accepted, detail and candidate bytes; decode with the Windows TOML codec for the decoded checks.
